schedulerRules: Each wave fires once per attempt unless restored from a later checkpoint.
A wave waits when the active regular-enemy cap would be exceeded.
Boss-level regular enemies are restricted to the approach zones unless a boss contract explicitly summons minions.
Leaving an activation range may sleep enemies but does not silently count them as defeated.
Checkpoint restoration clears post-checkpoint scheduler state and keeps pre-checkpoint waves completed.
Difficulty changes composition counts without removing attack telegraphs.

zones.beatPlan: A broad safe meadow gives room to walk, run, stop and swap heroes. Low coin arcs establish the normal jump shape.
A single short gap, a low step and a downhill slope teach speed preservation with no lethal consequence beneath them.
Camp Critters patrol separated platforms. The first one is isolated so side contact and stomp timing are readable.
A Shellback beside breakable blocks demonstrates retracting, kicking and shell-driven destruction.
After the checkpoint, terrain alternates between upper ledges and a lower creek path. Both remain visible so route choice feels intentional.
A rope bridge, Spike Beetles and one Camp Sentry require moving between high and low cover while maintaining forward rhythm.
A long rolling hill leads into three graduated gaps and a clean goal approach, combining speed, jump control and enemy reading.
Two broad hills show that downhill running increases practical jump reach while uphill travel slows the player.
An Acorn Bomber drops acorns onto flat ground, clearly showing its shadow and release timing.
Bombers patrol over a gap sequence where acorns roll downhill after landing.
Low branches force the player to release jump early or crouch-slide beneath them instead of holding every jump.
Inside the hollow oak, slopes become enclosed root ramps and acorns ricochet from wooden walls.
A Shellback can clear rolling acorns, but careless kicks send the shell back down the same slopes.
A sustained downhill run crosses alternating upper and lower platforms before a final leap through a falling-acorn curtain.
The bank entrance visibly crumbles when struck, establishing the visual language of soft dirt.
A Dirt Squirt travels beneath a transparent dirt strip before emerging onto safe ground.
Root lifts move slowly over shallow pits while Dirt Squirts force the player to change platforms.
Some soft walls reform after several seconds, creating temporary shortcuts but never trapping the player.
The crystal-root basin adds reflected silhouettes that reveal burrowing enemies before they emerge.
The return shaft combines vertical root lifts, Spike Beetles and reforming dirt ledges.
Two exits become visible near the surface: the obvious bank opening and a sealed root door opened by a clue sequence found earlier.
The first stair module rotates over solid flooring, teaching its timing without fall risk.
Hargold breaks a low reinforced block while Mebble reaches an alternate overhead switch; both methods rotate the same stairs.
Rotating stairs cross a narrow shaft with ledges beneath the first failed jumps.
Camp Sentry projectiles can strike tower switches, letting the player use enemy fire to change stair orientation.
The upper tower loses its outer wall, adding wind and moving hanging platforms while preserving the strict side plane.
Three stair modules rotate on offset cycles while Sentry fire passes through shield openings.
A rapid lift carries the player through the bell structure into the final mechanism chamber.
A Sentry fires across a wide bridge with multiple cover blocks and no pit beneath the lane.
Its shot breaks a brittle wall and reveals a normal-coin cache, establishing projectiles as tools.
Two staggered lanes cross moving bridge sections over a shallow ravine.
Wooden cover degrades after repeated hits, so waiting indefinitely gradually removes safety.
After the checkpoint, rotating shield plates redirect shots diagonally into mechanisms.
Shellbacks patrol the same lanes, creating a choice between stopping shells or using them to clear Sentries.
The last bridge raises section by section as three Sentry switches are struck during continuous forward movement.
A low wind pocket slows falling over solid ground, previewing glide behavior.
Mebble can glide to an upper ledge while Hargold rides a nearby lift to the same destination.
A wide canopy gap requires either controlled gliding or a timed sequence of grounded lifts.
Low branches require closing the glide to drop beneath them and reopening after passing.
Wind alternates direction in visible leaf-filled pockets, changing horizontal drift.
Acorn Bombers and moving branches force the player to choose when to sacrifice height for safety.
A long aerial descent threads three branch gates before both hero routes converge at the goal tree.
A clear signpost and camera framing show both branches before commitment: canopy above, creek below.
The first obstacle on each branch previews its rule without lethal pressure: drifting branch above, floating log below.
Canopy asks for timed aerial transfers; creek asks for shell control across moving logs.
Canopy branches begin to fall after landing; creek logs sink under sustained weight.
Each route crosses the other visually, allowing players to see missed rewards without switching branches.
After rejoining, wind pushes hanging logs while Shellbacks and Acorn Bombers occupy alternating elevations.
A collapsing cliff forces rapid transfers between high branches and low logs, summarizing both routes.
The entrance shows one root moving after a harmless step, then returning to its original position.
Lantern spores briefly outline concealed root platforms over solid ground.
The player crosses a dark pit using roots whose next positions are previewed by drifting spores.
Some roots rotate nearby roots when weighted, making route order matter.
The root heart pulses on a fixed rhythm, alternately revealing platforms and waking enemies.
Shellback weight can hold one root in place while the player crosses another; Sentry shots can illuminate spores from a distance.
A rapid sequence asks the player to memorize three previewed root positions before the cavern goes dark.
The gate exterior uses familiar slopes and Shellbacks at higher density, signaling a mastery course rather than a tutorial.
A reinforced gate opens when a Sentry shot is redirected through a rotating root reflector.
The outer ruins combine rotating stairs with wind-exposed gaps and enemy fire.
Living roots repair destroyed platforms unless their glowing anchor is broken.
Inside the gate, the route descends around a rotating stone core while poison-free root sap rises as a nonlethal timing pressure.
A final hallway combines falling branches, Sentry switches, Shellback block chains and a short glide/lift split.
The hallway opens directly into the circular root arena; the same reflectors and anchors become boss mechanics.
A wide beach introduces shallow water, dry sand and low rocks while the first tide marker rises harmlessly beside solid ground.
The tide covers one low shelf but leaves an overhead ledge available, teaching that the route changes rather than simply becoming blocked.
Two short channels require entering water, swimming with a gentle current and exiting onto wet stone without losing forward momentum.
A second tide reaches higher and activates Tidebiters only while submerged, forcing the player to choose between an early low route and a later high route.
After the checkpoint, a collapsing sandbar creates a temporary lower shortcut while floating driftwood becomes the stable route during high tide.
Camp Sentry fire crosses a tidal channel while Shellbacks patrol the exposed rock shelves, making water level determine available cover.
A long run across stepping rocks ends with the tide surging behind the player and lifting a driftwood bridge toward the goal bluff.
A shallow cave mouth shows a current carrying loose shells toward a broad safe pool.
The player swims through one short current tube with an immediate air pocket at the far end.
A longer tube reverses direction after a warning pulse, requiring shelter behind stone ribs rather than fighting the current continuously.
Bubble vents lift lightweight objects and enemies, opening routes but popping when touched by the player.
After the checkpoint, current boundaries become visible through drifting sand, and air pockets move vertically on buoyant stone chambers.
Tidebiters, bubble-lifted Shellbacks and narrow current shelters combine without introducing a new enemy type.
The final tunnel alternates current direction twice while the player transfers between three rising air bells before bursting onto the shore.
The entrance shows two adjacent channels at different heights so the effect of the first floodgate is immediately readable.
A large lever drains a safe chamber and exposes a lower walkway with no time pressure.
The second gate fills one route while draining another, forcing the player to read level geometry before committing.
Camp Sentry shots pass through glass tubes and can strike mechanisms the player cannot physically reach.
After the checkpoint, the grotto remembers both earlier gate states and presents different but completable routes for each combination.
Shellbacks break coral shutters while remote shots change the current around them, combining enemy tools with persistent state.
The final room displays the normal exit above water and a sealed deep-current tunnel whose gate depends on an earlier optional setting.
A low mirror rotates over solid ground and powers a nearby lift when its beam touches a receiver.
A second mirror must be held briefly while the lift rises, teaching the delay between alignment and machinery response.
Open breakwater platforms introduce broad waves with clear background telegraphs and safe masonry niches.
Sentry shots can rotate jammed mirrors, while wave impacts temporarily change the angle of unsecured reflectors.
After the checkpoint, the outer tower combines vertical climbing, horizontal fence movement and mirrors mounted on moving frames.
Two offset wave lanes and three mirrors create a compact route puzzle under pressure without adding a new rule.
The final beam opens the bell chamber and overloads the bell machinery below.
The first coral shelf flexes over shallow water and clearly recovers after the player steps off.
Two shelves demonstrate that Hargold sinks them faster while Mebble gains more height from their rebound.
A chain over deep water requires transferring before a shelf submerges completely.
Currents begin sliding submerged shelves sideways, making weight and timing alter both height and position.
After the checkpoint, cracked coral can be deliberately broken to reach lower routes but never reforms during the same attempt.
Shellbacks add temporary weight, Bubblebloom can lift them away, and Tidebiters occupy the submerged recovery lanes.
The final reef chain drifts toward a waterfall edge while the player chooses rapid upper jumps or controlled lower transfers.
The ferry begins in calm water and visibly tilts as the player walks from side to side.
A low arch requires standing at the rear to raise the bow, teaching weight control without enemies.
The first current gate accelerates the ferry while one Camp Critter boards from a dock.
Shellbacks can be kicked off, used as counterweights or allowed to strike gate mechanisms mounted along the route.
After the checkpoint, the ferry splits into two linked rafts that tilt independently but share forward speed.
Sentry fire, boarding enemies and alternating undertow gates require controlling weight while clearing the deck.
The final current releases the ferry down a steep water chute, where shifting to the correct raft determines the landing platform.
A small bell drains one safe chamber while filling a visible adjacent chamber.
A two-room example teaches that each bell has a fixed tone and always affects the same connected spaces.
The first traversal requires ringing a bell, crossing the drained room and reaching shelter before the returned current arrives.
Wraith wisps emerge only inside flowing water and can be redirected by changing which room carries the current.
After the checkpoint, three tones must be used in sequence, but the bell engravings and pipe colors make the state readable.
Shellbacks hold floor switches while wisps patrol active currents, combining state memory with enemy placement.
The final nave rings all bells in a repeating pattern as the player climbs through rooms that alternately flood and drain.
A moonbeam illuminates one safe swimming lane while surrounding currents visibly pull loose particles toward hazards.
The first shadowed lane contains an obvious air pocket that appears only when the beam passes over it.
A pressure descent compresses bubbles and increases downward pull, but broad ledges allow the player to learn the changed movement.
Rotating moon mirrors sweep the beam across several current lanes, making visibility itself part of route timing.
After the checkpoint, pressure chambers alternate between deep pull and buoyant release, transforming the same route geometry.
Tidebiters, spectral wisps and collapsing air pockets combine while the beam reveals only one safe solution at a time.
The final ascent follows a fast-moving moonbeam through a vertical undertow shaft and exits beneath the boss lighthouse.
The lower lighthouse combines shallow tide cycles with familiar mirror receivers in a stable stone interior.
A safe flooded shaft demonstrates that lightning briefly reverses all vertical currents before the player faces lethal gaps.
The first tower test uses tide timing, moving coral shelves and mirror-controlled doors in a compact sequence.
Spectral currents begin carrying enemies and projectiles between floors, turning prior hazards into route tools.
After the midpoint, the outer tower breaks open and storm waves rotate the lighthouse mechanisms while the player climbs.
The final approach combines ferry-like balance, bell-state water transfer and a fast vertical current reversal.
The lantern lens shatters, revealing Wraithbound and transforming the tower top into the boss arena.
A broad dune shows one dark shade band crossing soft sand while coins remain safely on the firm shaded strip.
A low crystal fin can be struck to rotate its shadow over a harmless sand pocket, teaching cause and effect without a pit.
The first real crossing requires rotating a fin, then moving with its slow shade sweep before the sand gives way.
Two fins overlap their shadows, creating a stable platform only where both bands intersect; Shellbacks can rotate the lower fin remotely.
After the checkpoint, wind slowly turns unsecured fins and introduces moving shade routes rather than fixed ones.
Camp Sentry shots, sinking sand and Acorn Bomber impacts combine so enemy attacks can alter the safe path as well as threaten the player.
The final dune face collapses in sunlight while a chain of rotating crystals builds a moving staircase toward the goal arch.
A blue crystal rings beside a blue platform over solid ground, showing the platform appear and fade on a generous timer.
Two tones activate separate stair steps, with engraved wave symbols identifying which crystal controls each surface.
A short cavern crossing requires striking a tone and reaching its platform before the resonance ends.
Echo pulses now travel through crystal chains, allowing one strike to activate distant surfaces in a readable order.
After the checkpoint, tones can overlap and produce a third harmonic platform only while both source crystals remain active.
Shellbacks carry impacts through crystal chains while Spike Beetles occupy the stable ledges between timed surfaces.
The final chamber becomes a seven-note ascent where each landing triggers the next resonant step toward daylight.
The level opens with a real platform and a harmless mirrored copy above solid sand; dust passes through the false image while coins rest on the real one.
A second example uses bird shadows and drifting sand to reveal which of two ledges is solid.
The first canyon requires committing to a running jump toward the real ledge while the decoy dissolves during takeoff.
Mirages begin copying moving platforms with a slight delay, making motion timing another readable clue.
After the checkpoint, wind gusts stretch and compress mirage images, while real platforms retain stable shadows.
Acorn Bombers, Shellbacks and delayed platform copies combine so the player must preserve momentum while reading genuine collision cues.
The final sprint crosses a chain of alternating real and false dunes as a sand wall advances from behind.
A single prism splits sunlight into two beams that power two adjacent lifts over safe ground.
A movable prism demonstrates that beam angles remain fixed and receivers illuminate before machinery activates.
The first tower shaft requires carrying or pushing a prism between floors to power alternating elevators.
Rotating shutters interrupt portions of the split beam, creating timed safe windows without changing the underlying geometry.
After the checkpoint, Camp Sentry shots rotate mounted prisms while the player climbs fences across the tower exterior.
Three receivers, two shutters and one movable prism combine in a compact final mechanism puzzle under projectile pressure.
The completed beam network opens the scarab vault and opens the glass-floor escape route.
A weak tailwind carries coins across solid ground and visibly lengthens a basic jump.
One glass fin rotates the same wind upward, lifting the player gently onto a safe ledge.
The first ravine crossing requires using an upward gust to reach a rope, then releasing into a tailwind-assisted landing.
Wind fins begin redirecting currents between horizontal, upward and downward channels, changing both jumps and rope swing speed.
After the checkpoint, shattered fins create pulsing gusts instead of continuous streams and require release timing.
Acorn Bombers alter pendulum timing while Crystal Wisps occupy active wind lanes and Spike Beetles guard sheltered platforms.
The final ravine uses three ropes across alternating gust directions, ending with a long release through a crystal arch.
The lead sled moves slowly while a visible energy crystal powers its rail, and stepping between sleds shows their fixed link spacing.
A safe station switch routes energy to the rear sled, causing it to close the gap and teaching power distribution.
The first active rail section requires moving between sleds to avoid low arches while keeping at least one crystal socket powered.
Boarding enemies can occupy switches or add weight, and Shellbacks can be used to trigger track mechanisms at speed.
After the checkpoint, the caravan separates across parallel rails and energy routing changes which sled leads each segment.
Sentry fire, broken track gates and Acorn Bomber cargo impacts combine while the player chooses when to regroup the convoy.
The final descent sends all three sleds down converging rails, with one last energy transfer determining whether they land together at the goal depot.
A single strike returns one echo from the correct doorway while false doors remain silent.
A two-door example shows that distance determines echo delay and engraved rings identify the intended order.
The first tomb route requires striking two crystals and entering the door whose echoes return low then high.
Mirror corridors now repeat room geometry, but dust, enemy placement and echo direction distinguish the real route.
After the checkpoint, echoes persist between connected rooms and must be intentionally cancelled by damping crystals.
Crystal Wisps travel along active echoes while Shellbacks hold damping plates and Camp Sentries trigger remote tones.
The final burial hall plays a five-tone sequence while mirrored walls rotate, and each correct door removes one false corridor.
A distant shard impact breaks an unused platform while a clockwork warning lamp establishes the fixed strike interval.
A safe test lets the player stand beneath a marked ceiling and move away before the shard opens a lower route.
The first descent requires allowing one impact to destroy a floor, then catching a rope below instead of staying on the normal ledge.
Impact markers begin moving on quarry rails, so timing determines which of two platforms is destroyed.
After the checkpoint, prior destruction changes lift paths and exposes alternate anchor points for ropes.
Shellbacks, falling lifts and successive shard impacts combine as the player preserves the one bridge needed for the return climb.
The final shaft becomes a controlled collapse where each impact opens the next descent while removing the previous safe platform.
The outer vault uses shade-stabilized sand and a single prism receiver in a low-pressure introduction to the combined systems.
A safe chamber demonstrates that one resonant tone rotates the central light source and changes both shadows and beam routes.
The first fortress test combines mirage platforms with crystal shadows, requiring the player to identify the real surface before stabilizing it.
Wind channels now carry resonance pulses and Sentry projectiles between rooms, turning earlier hazards into remote tools.
After the midpoint, the central light fractures into three moving sources and prior room states determine which route remains open.
The final approach combines a rope crossing, timed resonance bridge, collapsing sand floor and three-prism lock without introducing a new rule.
The vault core absorbs every active beam, awakens the Luminite Golem and shatters the surrounding chamber into the battle arena.
A fixed cloud over solid ground visibly compresses beneath a Camp Critter, teaching that weight changes its height without immediate danger.
Three low clouds form a staircase above grass ledges; waiting too long lowers each step but every fall lands safely.
A shallow ravine requires crossing two sinking clouds before either descends below the far ledge.
Clouds now rebound when vacated, allowing a timed second jump; a Shellback can hold one cloud low to create a different route.
After the checkpoint, side wind shifts at clear flag markers and changes which face is easiest to wall-jump.
Buzzer flights, sinking clouds and alternating wall-jump shafts combine while stone balconies provide recovery pockets.
A long cloud chain sinks behind the player as a gust pushes toward the goal ridge, creating a fast but fully player-controlled finish.
A lightning flash solidifies one translucent block over safe floor while a countdown glow shows how long it will remain solid.
Two conductive blocks create a short stair only during the pulse; missing the timing drops the player onto a lower path.
A wall-jump shaft alternates which side is solid, requiring two clean transfers without introducing enemies.
A grounded rod lets the player strike or redirect a Sentry shot to trigger the pulse at a chosen time.
After the checkpoint, blue and gold circuits pulse on opposite phases, changing the safe surface rather than simply shortening timing.
Sky Gnats occupy the open gaps while player-triggered rods create temporary walls and ceilings.
The last tunnel becomes a long alternating wall corridor whose conductive sides appear in a readable left-right rhythm.
A broad tethered kite tilts gently under the player over safe scaffolding while coins show the rising edge.
Walking across the kite changes its angle and reveals that jumping from the high edge gives more distance.
Two kites overlap above a shallow canyon and require transferring when their high edges meet.
Acorn Bomber drops act as temporary weights; cutting one anchor converts a balancing platform into a controlled swing.
After the checkpoint, gust gates rotate the entire kite around its tether rather than only tilting it.
Bomb Birds, wall-jump masts and two linked kites require managing air space and platform angle together.
A three-kite relay climbs around the final tower while each released anchor changes the next platform position.
The tower rotates one quarter turn over solid flooring, visibly changing a shutter from wall to ceiling.
A low chamber asks the player to rotate once and wall-jump up the shutter that becomes vertical.
The first exterior opening exposes wind only after rotation; a sheltered center column prevents accidental falls.
Lightning rods lock one shutter in place while the rest of the chamber rotates around it.
After the checkpoint, rotation is driven by the storm mechanism above and occurs after clear three-beat telegraphs.
Gear Bots occupy rotating floors while Camp Sentry shots can energize rods from across the shaft.
The last ascent rotates two connected chambers in opposite directions before opening onto the roof escape platform.
A rain channel turns one small wheel over solid floor while its connected lift visibly rises.
Moving a short gutter reverses the wheel and lowers the same lift, teaching direct control.
A cistern crossing requires filling water beneath a buoyant platform and jumping off before the overflow pushes it away.
Two wheels share one rainfall stream, forcing a route choice between raising a platform and opening a gate.
After the checkpoint, gusts bend the rainfall sideways so gutters must be positioned before each wind cycle.
Wave Fins occupy flooded cisterns while Gear Bots turn dry backup cranks on adjacent ledges.
A cascading series of three reservoirs turns overflow from one chamber into the power source for the next.
Two slow gondolas hang over safe mountain terraces and visibly swing when the player lands near an edge.
A brake lever shortens the gap between cars while solid scaffolding remains beneath them.
The convoy crosses its first open ravine and asks the player to time a transfer as the cars swing together.
Loose cargo and Bomb Bird drops change individual car weight, altering both height and swing period.
After the checkpoint, the convoy splits at a junction and the player chooses a high combat route or low machinery route inside one continuous level.
Camp Chippers fire arcing wood chips across swinging cars while Sentries guard brake mechanisms.
The damaged final cable slopes downward and the player runs across cars that detach one at a time behind them.
Two doors remain visible while a pressure gauge changes; only one connection shifts and a window shows the destination.
The player toggles calm and charged states to return through the same small pair of rooms without hazards.
A three-room loop requires reading airflow ribbons to choose the door that leads upward.
Lantern Wisps drift toward the currently valid hidden vent while Crate Mimics punish rushing into apparently safe furniture rooms.
After the checkpoint, venting state creates temporary wall-jump surfaces from compressed cloud columns.
Door routing, hidden vents and moving cloud walls combine while the mansion slowly discharges toward the exterior.
The last pressure release opens every room into one continuous collapsing hallway toward the goal balcony.
A short coin trail ends in open air, but a falling raindrop splashes against an invisible platform over safe cloud ground.
The player jumps through mist to reveal a three-platform stair that remains visible for several seconds.
The first open gap requires revealing the landing with a projectile or controlled short jump before committing.
Lightning reveals entire connected condensation chains while heavy landings reveal only the contacted platform.
After the checkpoint, wind carries revealed mist away, making the platform shape readable but temporary.
Sky Gnats, Feather Drifts and narrow wall anchors require revealing the route while maintaining aerial control.
A lightning storm outlines a huge spiral of hidden platforms for one final upward circuit around the goal beacon.
The citadel entry combines one sinking cloud, one windbreak shutter and one harmless engine rotation to restate the world rules.
A maintenance room lets the player rotate a wind engine and watch a conductive wall move into wall-jump position.
The first exterior bridge combines cloud weight and crosswind while permanent stone alcoves provide recovery.
Archmage illusions reverse selected wind lanes, but flags and loose debris reveal the true direction before each change.
After the checkpoint, the citadel separates into rotating rings and the player must align rods, walls and lifts across two connected chambers.
Camp Sentries, Gear Bots, Shock Jellies and Bomb Birds interact with the machinery rather than appearing as unrelated pressure.
The last engine overload rotates the entire approach around the central arena and deposits the player at the boss door.
A harmless mirage duplicates a low rock over solid ground; walking through the false copy teaches that shimmer direction identifies the real object.
Three low glass-sand shelves appear during a slow heat pulse while every missed jump lands in a shallow safe trough.
The first dune gap requires committing to the real shelf before the mirage closes, with a permanent sandstone ledge as recovery.
Sirocco flags introduce a side gust that changes the safest jump arc without changing which shelves are real.
After the checkpoint, mirage copies move opposite their real platforms, turning observation into a timing challenge rather than simple recognition.
Acorn Bombers drop rolling hazards across two mirage bridges while Shellbacks can be used to test suspicious lower surfaces.
A long ridge run alternates visible and hidden shelves in a fixed rhythm while a sustained tailwind carries the player toward the oasis gate.
A single glass tile over a shallow chamber shows visible crack stages when a Camp Critter walks and the player lands on it.
The player chooses between preserving an upper coin route with soft landings or ground-slamming into a harmless lower room.
A glass bridge above a sand pit requires moving steadily because repeated landings break the same tile.
Rock Runts add weight to tiles; only Hargold ground slams can defeat them, but either hero can route around their break zones.
After the checkpoint, inverted glass ceilings fall as platforms when floor switches are struck.
Dirt Squirts emerge beneath weakened tiles while ceiling slabs create temporary shelter from shard rain.
A descending glass staircase breaks behind the player, revealing a parallel lower path through the temple exit.
A small sand basin fills beneath a fixed ledge, raising the player safely to a door before draining through a visible grate.
Two switches control separate inlet and outlet gates with no enemies or fatal pit beneath them.
A vertical shaft requires riding the sand level, wall-jumping between carved recesses and opening the outlet before the ceiling closes.
A Shellback can hold one pressure plate while the player reaches the second, creating an optional simultaneous-switch route.
After the checkpoint, dark sand flows sideways through wall channels and forms short-lived ramps instead of simply changing height.
Crawblers patrol the dry ledges while Dirt Squirts emerge from newly deposited sandbanks.
The last vault drains from top to bottom, forcing a controlled descent through doors that close behind the falling sand line.
Three furnace plates glow, warn and heat over solid surrounding stone, safely teaching the cycle.
A thermal lift rises during heating and returns during cooling above a shallow nonfatal trench.
A visible Compass Coin requires crossing heated plates and leaving before the next full furnace pulse.
Pistons extend during heating while a cooling valve pauses the cycle and drains the next channel.
After the checkpoint, the furnace lift shaft uses heat to accelerate upward and cooling to expose side platforms.
Reversing conveyors, Sentry fire and rolling Shellbacks share one synchronized machinery lane.
A controlled overload raises lava behind the player while steam vents become movement tools in the final sprint.
A low vane turns a gentle updraft sideways over solid ground and streamers clearly show the new direction.
Two broad spires let the player test updraft, tailwind and headwind jumps with safety nets below.
A narrow gap requires rotating the vane to a tailwind, then jumping before it slowly returns to neutral.
Camp Sentry shots can rotate distant vanes, allowing the player to redirect wind without standing beside the control.
After the checkpoint, paired vanes control upper and lower gust lanes independently.
Shardwing flyers cross the airspace while wall-jump shafts alternate between updraft and crosswind states.
Four spires form a single long aerial chain whose vanes must be set in sequence before the first resets.
A short sandstream carries the player over solid floor while arrow carvings show its speed and direction.
One gate raises the stream into an upper channel; missing the switch simply uses the lower safe path.
A long channel requires jumping between floating stone plates while the stream carries both player and enemies.
Shellbacks roll with the current and can hold side gates open after being kicked into weighted slots.
After the checkpoint, the stream accelerates downhill and occasional reverse eddies create brief backward sections.
Prism Scarabs shed crystal fragments into the stream while overhead crushers create alternating high and low routes.
The stream divides repeatedly around a collapsing ruin, then reunites in a fast final chute toward the goal platform.
A small sun disk rotates one shadow bridge between floor and wall over a safe chamber.
Two disk faces clearly map to two bridge positions, allowing repeated experimentation without enemies.
The player rotates a room so a wall-jump shaft becomes a floor route, then must return the disk to exit.
Camp Sentry beams can illuminate remote disk faces while Hargold-only blocks reveal alternate rotation handles.
After the checkpoint, linked disks rotate in opposite directions and retain their state between adjacent rooms.
Shadow bridges, falling sand and Spike Pods combine across three connected chambers with visible state diagrams.
The final solar hall rotates twice during one continuous traversal, changing floor, walls and bridges around the player.
The Wraith passes over a short safe trench and briefly outlines three buried platforms before they fade.
A second route remains above solid sand while footprints continue to mark each hidden platform.
The player crosses a longer hidden bridge using fading footprints and fixed wind-chime timing.
The Wraith now doubles back, revealing one route while erasing another; the correct path is indicated by sand flowing toward the exit.
After the checkpoint, the player can use switches to redirect the Wraith through upper or lower channels.
Spike Pods occupy visible islands while Lantern Wisps reveal only the nearest hidden platform.
The Wraith circles a vast hollow, exposing a complete spiral route one segment ahead of the player before collapsing the center.
The palace entrance uses one short mirage bridge and a permanent floor diagram to remind the player of the world’s visual language.
A controlled sand basin and wind vane open the first gate without enemy pressure.
A glass-floor corridor combines soft landings with a side gust and a visible recovery route beneath it.
Two sun disks rotate shadow bridges around a flowing sand chamber while Sentry beams act as remote light sources.
After the checkpoint approach, the palace begins sinking and room states persist as sand floods connecting passages.
Mirage shelves, reversing sand currents and rotating obelisk beams form the final fortress ascent.
The player outruns a collapsing throne corridor, enters the antechamber and sees the same obelisks arranged in the boss arena.
A shallow drift slows running but safely compresses beneath repeated movement, visibly becoming a firmer path.
The player ground-slams a marked drift over solid ground, creating a short ramp to an upper ledge.
A deep basin requires maintaining speed across packed snow or using the compacted ramp route.
Wormlets burrow through loose snow and leave temporary trenches that alter approach angles.
After the checkpoint, wind builds new drifts against walls and gradually covers low platforms.
Bounce Bunnies, changing drift heights and universal wall jumps combine across a stepped alpine slope.
A long uphill run alternates packed and loose lanes while snow accumulates behind the player and forms the final jump ramp.
A short black-ice strip over solid stone lets the player feel long braking distance with a padded wall at the end.
A gentle downhill teaches crouch sliding and slide jumping into a wide recovery platform.
A frozen gap requires preserving downhill speed, jumping late and using universal wall-jump recovery on the far face.
Reflections in the ice show Spike Beetles and falling icicles before their real bodies enter the playable lane.
After the checkpoint, cracked black ice can be broken by ground slams to reach slower lower routes.
Frost Hounds chase across alternating rough and slick surfaces while ceiling reflections announce icicle drops.
A long mirrored descent ends in a momentum-preserving slide jump across a widening cavern mouth.
A brief whiteout crosses a wide ledge while fixed rope knots and wall flags remain visible at close range.
The player climbs one rope during a mild gust with a solid floor beneath the entire route.
A wall-jump shaft alternates safe faces as crosswind arrows appear on nearby flags before each whiteout.
Powdergeist wisps form temporary wind shadows that reduce drift behind them.
After the checkpoint, rope anchors swing in the gust and preserve release momentum into wall jumps.
Snowblind Stalkers move only during the darkest whiteout beats while sound and footprints reveal their approach.
The last cliff face combines swinging ropes, alternating wall-jump markers and one sustained whiteout to reach the summit gate.
A small bell strike shakes harmless powder from a ceiling and reveals a frozen platform beneath it.
Two bells rotate one stair drum between clearly marked positions above a solid floor.
A bell pulse releases a snow shelf that becomes a moving ramp before settling into the lower corridor.
Camp Sentry projectiles can strike bells remotely while Hargold-only blocks expose alternate clappers.
After the checkpoint, the large tower bell causes two connected chambers to rotate in opposite directions.
Falling icicles, rotating walls and Sentry fire combine across the upper mechanism without introducing a boss.
The player rings the crown bell, outruns a descending snow collapse and rides the loosened bell frame down the exterior.
A small controlled snow release covers a trench and creates a safe ramp over solid ground.
The player opens one release gate and watches snow fill a low path while the upper ledge remains usable.
The main avalanche begins at moderate speed, requiring route choices but allowing brief shelter stops.
Gate levers divert snow into upper or lower channels, changing whether later walls are buried or exposed.
After the checkpoint, the avalanche overtakes the foreground and creates temporary vertical snow faces for wall jumps.
Frost Hounds and rolling ice boulders enter from side chutes while the player uses the avalanche-built terrain.
The player opens three release gates in sequence, building the final ramp moments before the avalanche fills the canyon.
